findings.title: Swapped lightness values change the light-theme color of the embedded-post author link
findings.body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The pattern used throughout this PR keeps the light-theme branch unchanged and adds a complementary dark-theme branch (100−X), i.e. this should have become `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` — exactly as done for the same 30% case in common/base/topic-post.scss line 15 of this PR. Instead the committed line is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`: the two values are swapped. Light themes now render this link far lighter than before, and dark themes get a dark 30%-lightness gray instead of the intended 70% gray, hurting readability in both themes.

findings.title: custom-message-length uses swapped lightness values, changing the light theme and conflicting with desktop
findings.body: `.custom-message-length` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. In this same PR the identical class in desktop/modal.scss (line 94) was correctly converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, but the mobile file was changed to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` — the branches are swapped. Light-theme mobile now shows this hint text much darker than desktop/before, and dark-theme mobile shows it brighter than intended, so the flag-modal character-count hint is inconsistent between desktop and mobile.

findings.title: topic-map h3 lightness changed from 20% to 50% in the light branch instead of adding a dark branch
findings.body: `.topic-map h3` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. Per this PR's conversion rule it should become `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))` — which is exactly what desktop/topic-post.scss line 321 (the same selector) was changed to. The mobile file instead committed `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which lightens the heading in the light theme (a change this PR is not supposed to make) and gives dark themes a 50% gray where 80% was intended, diverging from desktop.

findings.title: group-member-info .name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. Following the PR's rule it should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, but the committed line is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This silently lightens the member name in light themes and gives dark themes a 50% gray instead of the correct 70% complement.

findings.title: group-member-info .name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
findings.body: Same issue as desktop/user.scss: `.group-member-info .name` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and should have been converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, but the committed value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light theme now renders the name lighter than before and the dark theme gets the wrong complement (50% instead of 70%).

findings.title: Missed conversion: category badge-notification still uses scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)
findings.body: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still reads `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`, the exact pattern this PR eliminates everywhere else (six other occurrences in this same file were converted). On dark themes, where $primary is near-white, this badge count stays blindingly bright instead of being dimmed to a gray derived from $secondary like the rest of the UI. It should be `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`.
